beats.care: If your family is from a drought-hit taluka, ask your college about zero-challan before October 30. Already paid? Ask for a refund.
beats.what: 65,200 SPPU students have filled exam forms without paying, through a 'zero-challan' facility. Across 26 universities, 2,40,365 students have used it so far.
beats.why: Weak rain has hit farm families. The state listed 305 drought-affected talukas and told universities to waive exam fees there.

cards.body: The government expects the number to cross five lakh once all exam forms are in.
cards.caption: students across 26 universities helped so far

cards.body: Universities that collected fees are refunding eligible students. COEP Tech and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth have started refunds. Stuck? Call your university's published helpline.
cards.title: Already paid the fee?

opts: Fill the exam form without paying the fee
cards.q: What does the 'zero-challan' facility let a student do?
cards.why: It lets eligible students from drought-hit areas submit exam forms with no exam fee.

cards.body: The list of drought-hit talukas grew from 265 to 305, so more students became eligible than first planned.

cards.q: Should fee waivers be upfront, not refunds?

watch: The state says exam forms are due by October 30, and expects over five lakh students to use the waiver.
